reason: Not refuted, but the gain is small. The claim holds: files submitted up to 29 Sep 23:59Z score about 7 h later (latency 6.7-7.6 h), so the 23:27Z snapshot misses them. kaggle_api_extended.py l.2310-2332 writes a fixed <competition>.zip, and download_file l.5752-5754 creates the folder with os.makedirs, so one timestamped folder per call works. It is read-only, runs after the deadline, is calibration only and needs no submit or OK, so R1-R10 and R8 do not apply. It does not change the private score. Two limits. (1) It adds less to the (c) tie read than claimed. Many LATER x138 copies (after #37/#38, 26 Sep 20:0xZ) are already on the board: the late-copy windows logged at CONTEXT l.2033/2048/2131/2214/2240 have 15-17 each. So the 'between earlier and later copies' case can be classified from the 23:27Z snapshot. The late rows mainly catch teams whose public score changed in the last ~8 h, which fixes the copy set and the 0.955-0.957 set of the unrounded-order read. (2) It is partly redundant: the Public tab can still be read after the private reveal and is final then. The hourly saves only hedge the case where the CLI download switches to private. Side finding: the (d) board check ('our Score == max over F AND top-50 differs from the 23:30Z snapshot') can fire wrongly on 30 Sep 00-08Z. Late public rows reshuffle the top-50, and our public max 0.954 may equal our private max.
fix: Add to v2 (d): on each hourly read on 30 Sep (00:15Z until the private board is confirmed), also run `python -m kaggle competitions leaderboard biohub-cell-tracking-during-development -d -p experiments/private_read/lb_<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>/` (one folder per call, 3 retries with 60-120 s backoff, never overwrite). After the reveal, also save one read of the Public tab (browser, read-only) as the final public board. Also key the switch to the private board on competition_submissions privateScore being non-empty for #37/#38 (or on the Private tab), not on the top-50 differing from the snapshot. Calibration only, never a finals input; no OK needed.
realistic_gain: 0 on the private score. Calibration: a more complete x138-copy set and 0.955-0.957 set for the tie read and the unrounded-order read. It also prevents a false 'private board appeared' call on 30 Sep. Cost: about 1 CLI call per hour and a few KB.
